cohort: 688 single, nonanomalous infants born at 22+0-25+6 weeks gestation at a tertiary center in Australia
finding: For periviable breech infants, vaginal birth was associated with reduced odds of survival compared to vaginal cephalic birth, while cesarean section improved survival for breech infants > 24 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: Vaginal breech birth had higher odds of very low Apgar scores, stillbirth, and neonatal death compared to cesarean breech births.
